description: Hajiaghayi-Sorkin Algorithm A with deterministic ties and the paper's printed True iff positive_degree < negative_degree rule.

source.title: The Satisfiability Threshold of Random 3-SAT Is at Least 3.52
source.chapter: Thresholds of Random k-SAT, Encyclopedia of Algorithms, Chapter 423, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_423
source.printed_assignment_rule: set v True if positive_degree < negative_degree and False otherwise

input.encoding: [n,m,3*m signed one-based literals grouped in formula order]
input.clause_rule: Each input clause contains exactly three nonzero literals on distinct variables; duplicate clauses are permitted.

contract.degrees: For each unset variable, count positive i and negative j occurrences in the current residual formula.
contract.selection: Any pure variable (i=0 or j=0) takes priority; choose the lowest variable ID. Otherwise maximize (abs(i-j), i+j) lexicographically, then choose the lowest variable ID among variables with that score.
contract.assignment: Preserve Algorithm A: set the chosen variable True iff i<j, otherwise False. Positive literal v is satisfied by True; negative literal -v is satisfied by False.
contract.unit_propagation: After each free variable assignment, repeatedly set the first residual unit clause in original formula order true.
contract.reduction: Delete satisfied clauses and remove each assigned literal's negation from all other clauses. Stop immediately if any clause becomes empty. No backtracking.
contract.completion: Continue free choices until every variable is assigned. If no empty clause was generated, report success.
contract.output: [success_bit, assignment[0..n)] as little-endian signed-i64 words; values are 1, -1, or 0 (unset on failure).

workspace.meaning: Fixed residual clauses, lengths, flags, degree counters, assignments, and staged output for n<=12 and m<=32.
